_comment: Content assertions for each patch. `must_contain` and `must_not_contain` are plain
substrings checked against the patch file itself, before it is applied.
This exists because two patches were wrong in ways that 'applies cleanly' could not
detect. 0003 was truncated to 2 of its 4 files and applied fine, doing nothing. 0005 was
captured while 0004 was still applied to the same file, so it silently carried 0004's
change too; applying the pair left 0005's own guard out, the build failed exactly as
before, and apply_air_patches.py reported 'skipped (already applied)'. A duplicated patch
is worse than a truncated one, because it reports success.
`must_not_contain` is the load-bearing half: it is what catches duplication.

0001-restartable-engine.patch.why: Split EngineMain::shutdown() into per-session teardown plus shutdownProcess(), so the engine can be left and re-entered in one process.

0002-restart-selftest.patch.why: Add -restartselftest: two EngineMain sessions back to back, exiting after script loading.

0003-restart-realsession.patch.why: Add -restartrealtest: two sessions running real frames, quitting via FTX::System->quit().

0004-sdl-include-path.patch.why: Add A.I.R.'s bundled SDL include dir; MSVC needs <SDL/SDL.h>, which only framework/include provides.

0005-stdcxxfs-guard.patch.why: Do not link stdc++fs under MSVC; it is a GCC/MinGW library and does not exist there.

0010-stringtraits-decl-order.patch.why: Move the StringTraits declaration above StringTemplate and qualify the two getUnicode call sites. Pure reordering plus AIR's own qualification idiom; it also subsumes the removed 0009.
